transcript.text: Our Henry has gone a bit weak and sounds rough, sort of rattly growl instead of the normal hum. It's about 12 years old. Bags and filter are new. Worth fixing?

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. To answer your question first: at 12 years old, it can be worth fixing if the issue is just a blockage or a simple part like a belt, but if the motor itself has failed, it may not be cost-effective. The most common cause after changing filters is a blockage in the airway (hose or floorhead) which forces the motor to work harder and sound rough. Could you please detach the hose from the main body and look through it, as well as check the wand and the neck where the floorhead attaches? Please let me know if you find any debris stuck inside.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I've had a look and dropped a coin through the hose and it goes straight through, so there's no blockage there. Both the hose end and the head are weak, though.

The "rattly growl" suggests either a blockage deep in the cyclone/bin inlet area or wear on the motor bearings (common after 12 years). To determine if it's worth fixing, I need to know exactly which Henry model you have, as internal parts and labour costs vary significantly between models. Could you please check the rating plate on the main body for the model number?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The label on the bottom says HVR 200-22. Is that the information you needed?

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. To separate these: please detach the hose again, switch it on briefly for a few seconds (keep your face away), and listen closely. Does the rattle come from deep inside the motor casing, or does it sound like air struggling through a blockage? Also, if you can see into the bin inlet, is there any visible debris stuck in the cyclone assembly?

Yes, I hope that's what you needed. I've switched it on briefly with the hose off, and it sounds like a rough growl from the motor itself rather than air struggling through something. Now that you ask, there's also a hot, burning electrical smell after a few minutes, and when I looked at the exhaust grille on top in the dark hall I saw sparks flickering inside.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Stop using the vacuum immediately. Do not plug it in again. The combination of a rough growl from the motor itself, a burning smell, and visible sparks inside the casing suggests an internal electrical fault—likely worn carbon brushes arcing against the commutator or damaged windings. This is a serious safety hazard that cannot be fixed by cleaning or simple owner checks. Given it is 12 years old and has suffered this type of failure, it is generally not cost-effective to repair; you should contact Henry vacuum customer support for advice on replacement or disposal.
